newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinea and Solomons to share border force.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea and Solomons to share border force.

text.p: Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands have agreed to establish joint border surveillance, Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said on Wednesday.

Under the agreement, PNG defence forces would be based on border posts in the Solomon Islands, allowing them to police the movement of Bougainville sessionist rebels between Bougainville island and the Solomons, he told a news conference.
The agreement with Solomon Islands Prime Minister Solomon Mamaloni was reached at the weekend, as Chan returned from the state funeral of Marshall Islands president Amata Kabua.
"Our meeting...is a demonstration of our resolve in seeking a lasting solution (on Bougainville)," Chan said.
Bougainville Revolutionary Army rebels, who have been fighting a bloody eight-year secessionist war, have been accused by PNG of using the Solomon Islands to hide out and win support.
The western islands of the Solomons are a short canoe ride from resource-rich Bougainville island, which lies 800 km (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby.
Tensions between the two countries heightened recently after members of the PNG security force were reported to have crossed into the Solomon Islands to pursue rebel forces.
Chan said the agreement would also allow for a third party to be involved in border surveillance. The identity of that party would be finalised at a later date.
He wanted the border arrangements put in place as soon as possible and said a solution to the Bougainville crisis would remain a top priority for his government.
